wa_coexist_boulder.blurb: Coexist Boulder is a single roadside block in the Skykomish Valley on the west side of the Cascades, and it is the bigger of the two boulders that make up the Hideout Boulders. It stands just up a path, only a few strides from the gravel road, so once you arrive there is no further walking. Sixteen problems are packed onto it. The bulk of them sit around V5, with a few in the V3 to V4 range, a couple of easy V0 lines, and a small top end reaching V7. It suits a short session for strong boulderers rather than a full day out.

wa_d_coyote_wall.blurb: Coyote Wall is one of the five named sections of the Sunshine Wall in Echo Basin at Frenchman Coulee, near Vantage. It is a stretch of basalt pillars that breaks into stacked columns, lying beyond the King Pins end of the cliff and short of the Near End. The sixteen routes are mostly trad with a few bolted lines, spanning about 5.6 to 5.11 with a cluster around 5.10. Expect an uncrowded, somewhat rough wall rather than a polished one: loose rock is mentioned, protection bolts are sparse, and few parties visit, so it suits experienced leaders who like to be alone.

wa_dishman_bouldering_wall.blurb: This small, tucked-away boulder wall sits in the Dishman Hills on the southeast side of Spokane. It was opened up around 2017 and holds sixteen problems spread nearly evenly from V0 through the mid grades, with a few harder ones up to V7, so beginners and strong boulderers can both find something. The lines are fun but contrived, with plenty of linkups and eliminates, which makes it a handy circuit for training. It can be dirty, some topouts are mossy, and a brush helps. There is no established trail to the base; plan on a short bushwhack from the car.
wa_dishman_bouldering_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the Camp Caro lot or the standard Dishman lot off East Appleway.

wa_fee_demo_wall.blurb: Fee Demo Wall is a tall, slabby granite face on the north side of Stegosaurus Butte, in the Middle Fork Snoqualmie valley close to North Bend. It sits just off the valley's river trail. Ten sport and six trad routes climb the slabs, spanning roughly 5.7 to 5.12, with the largest group in the 5.10 range. Several lines run to three pitches, and a longer rope makes the descents easier. The wall is still being cleaned and bolted, so expect a mix of fresh and older routes. It appeals to climbers who enjoy delicate slab work.

wa_martian_slab.blurb: Martian Slab is the large slab you can see above Orchard Rock when you stand in the parking area at Peshastin Pinnacles State Park, near Wenatchee and Leavenworth. Its sixteen routes split evenly between trad and sport, running from about 5.6 to 5.11 with the heaviest concentration in the 5.6 to 5.9 range. That makes it friendly to newer leaders while still offering a few harder bolted lines. Climbing here is slab and friction work, including a two-pitch line that crosses the face. A maintained trail from the lot leads to the base, so the walk is easy.

wa_madsen_s_ledge.blurb: Madsen's Ledge is a long, wide ledge at the east end of the Central Wall on Index's Upper Town Wall, about one pitch above the ground. Short, mostly single-pitch climbs start from it, ten bolted and six on gear, and several longer wall routes also pass through it. The grade range is steep for a crag: a couple at 5.8, a few around 5.10, then mostly 5.11 and 5.12 with a handful of 5.13s. Reaching the ledge means climbing the first pitch of a wall route, or using iron rungs at its east end, so it is not a casual stop for beginners.
